title: Evolve CIMA Frame Review | The Premium Surprise Nobody Saw Coming

takeaways.text: Packaging is almost plastic-free; the through-axles, seatpost wedge and hardware are cleanly machined and anodised, CeramicSpeed headset bearings are included, and the manual reads like a premium Western brand's.
Fully internal routing, a BSA 68 mm threaded shell with aluminium inserts, a UDH hanger and an immaculate headset seat; only one fork brake mount looked like it needed facing.
The Kreuza bar routes hoses through a wide internal opening for an easier bend, uses a standard computer mount, and comes with plugs so it can also run lines externally on another bike.
Weighed uncut: frame 775 g, fork about 363 g and seatpost 162 g; the Kreuza handlebar was 321 g with cap and zip tie. The frame size is not stated.
Borescope inspection found smooth internal surfaces with no ripples or layer shift, cleanly drilled rivnut holes and tidy bonding at the stay joints.

disclosure: No supply arrangement is stated; the description links Evolve's store, quotes a US$3,300 frameset, wheel and bottle bundle, and links a discount-code page and Patreon.
summary: Engineer's unboxing, weigh-in and borescope inspection of a CIMA road frameset and Kreuza handlebar before building it.
